rules: Table0x559c10..0x55a3cc has99 rows of20 bytes: id@0, callback@4, group byte@8, cached graphics-object pointer@12, dirty low byte@16; upper bytes are not reinterpreted.
0x4ea7a0 linearly compares row IDs and returns row index or-1; rows0/100 exist with null callbacks, IDs13/97 are absent.

Open0x4ea460 and ID-activity query0x4ea6f0 admit unsigned1..99 then require lookup success; this does not add a lookup guard to other slot helpers. Table membership alone does not authorize sentinel opening.
The cached graphics object and dirty flag are distinct from the classic224-byte window object and84-byte sidecar.
In main state10, opening IDs1/2/18/14/20/17 returns0; other guards and table lookup still apply.
For a nonzero requested row group, if restore flag0xc1dd94 is0, it is assigned the Boolean result of0x4ea6f0(1). This helper is an activity query, not an allocator.
Group2 changes primary slot0xc2056c to the requested ID, sets its dirty byte1 and clears secondary slot0xc20570; an unchanged primary returns0.

For groups0/1, lookup of current primary must succeed. If current primary is nonzero and group2, clear both slots before assigning slots[group]; otherwise update only the differing slot. A changed selection sets dirty1 and returns1.
0x4eae60 calls open(1) when the restore flag is nonzero, then clears that flag. These are alternate row group rules, not classic group bitmasks.
close(100) clears both active slots. If previous secondary was1, it returns1 immediately; otherwise a bit4 flag at0x7286b7 determines whether to call restore helper.

For ordinary IDs, close rejects invalid or unregistered rows. A matching group2 primary clears both slots, optionally restores id1 and returns0. A failed group2 primary comparison falls through to the group-indexed comparison at 4ea62c. For group2 that address is the adjacent word0xc20574.

A match in the group-indexed branch clears that word and returns1, with restoration subject to group and previous secondary. Groups0/1 normally address the two active slots. See the selected historical rules below.
Close does not itself call a graphics-object cleanup; inactive callback processing is a separate path.
0x4ea660 with an admitted nonzero ID below100 clears each slot that differs from that ID; its Boolean return follows the source comparisons, not a general success contract.
0x4ea6b0(2) tests either slot nonzero; other arguments index the slot base directly without a source bounds guard. Complete caller-domain validation remains open.
0x4ea3e0 clears0xc450a8,0xf5f050,0xc1dd94 only; it is not a generic clear-all active-window operation.
0x4e94d0 receives an active/inactive value, per-business descriptor, optional initializer and flags; it looks up descriptor id at+0x10.
For inactive input0, if the row graphics cache is nonzero, call0x40a090(cache) and clear it. If dirty was nonzero, clear dirty and return2 exactly once; otherwise return0.

For active input with no cached object, call0x4ea7c0 using descriptor geometry/style, write cache, play source sound and call an optional initializer. The callback is invoked after the creation attempt even if it returned0; then the cache is re-read and zero returns0.

Before input handling, assembly0x4e9623 binds ECX to graphicsObject+0x170 and calls0x4033d0(0); signed SETLE proves logicalValue<=0 returns0 from this helper. This is not a generic input-consumed guard.
The helper resets hover-tab byte+0xa1 to0xff, inspects up to5 six-word tab records when tab-count is nonzero, records a hit, and on raw left-down changes selected-tab byte+0xa0.
It updates hovered window id0xc43828 when body hit succeeds and close-widget hover bit0x40 is absent. If flags&1 and close-widget result&1, it calls close(id) and plays the source close sound.

Observed helper return values0/1/2 mean skipped/no participation, participating, and one-shot inactive dirty cleanup respectively; the actual dispatcher that supplies active/inactive to every table callback is not yet closed.
After its active close-button branch calls close(id), this helper still returns1 in that invocation; it does not immediately substitute the inactive return2 path.
0x4e9d00 checks widget hit rectangle at descriptor+8/+12 through+width/+height; outside returns0.
On hit it starts mask0x40, then maps raw edge1/2 to masks1/4, held1/2 to2/8, repeat1/2 to0x10/0x20, and double edges0x10/0x20 to0x80/0x100.
The same raw mouse globals are reused as classic input, but bit encodings differ. For example alternate0x40 is ordinary hit, while classic0x40 is mode4 stored-coordinate hit.

0x4eac80 compares wrapped logical pointer coordinates to bounds; lower-bound helper0x4035a0 implements argument<=point. A nonnegative fifth argument also invokes a drawing helper; input hit calls use-1.
0x4ea170 only compares the global text-focus pointer0x60ff08 with its argument; it is not a window-active query.

Alternate id2 callback0x4e6b00 uses inactive return2 to query focus against0xc5f5fc, conditionally call0x445220(&0x60fda8), then clear0xc5f5fc. Its byte-bound body is retained in the647-entry map; the helper call is not expanded into an unproved reset policy.
0x4ea400 still processes shared work-context conditions and then calls classic driver0x46ab90; two framework state effects cannot be assumed independent merely because the UI tables differ.
Lookup direct-call subset now has6 verified sites in5 bodies; derived4ea740 is82 bytes, not a canonical dossier.
4ea740 toggles by row graphics-cache presence; its1/0 return ignores open/close results.

Existing461d00/461e00 snapshot the id1 activity flag only if restore flag0; deferred4eadc0 action3 invokes restore. The battle entry producer and selected ordinary frame ordering are bound in battle_action_and_timed_restore; actual table-callback dispatch remains open.

source_rules: Window 19 uses 0x564E93. The selected active path requires the selected item index at [EBP-4] to be nonnegative, the business row flag to equal 1, and ED560C bit 0 to be set. The business row uses [EBP-0x198] with stride 0x49FC.

The branch stores the selected low byte at ED1553, clears ED4364 and closes the current ID at 5FB0E8, which is 19 in the file. The row discriminator at 1123B0C plus the business row offset selects two ordered open calls, 29 then 30, for value 255. Other values select open 25.

Windows 19, 25 and 29 use the primary slot. Windows 1 and 30 use the secondary slot. The selected input bit path in window 29 closes the ID at 603748, which is 29 in the file, and opens 19 in the primary slot.

For window 29 with inactive input, the common helper clears the cached graphic when present and returns 2 after consuming a nonzero row mark. The selected result-2 branch handles ED5304 and requests close 30. The result-0 branch returns through the callback tail.

Opening a nonzero-group row with a clear restore flag records whether window 1 is active. Closing active secondary 30 requests the restore helper. With a nonzero flag the helper attempts open 1 and clears the flag afterward. Main state 10 denies open 1.
